_spec.purpose: The self-improvement ledger. The retro phase records what a run LEARNED about making decks, and the next run's directors room and copy chamber are handed the instincts that have earned their place. This is the machine's craft memory, and it is the one ledger whose entries are about how to work rather than about what was published.
_spec.confidence_is_computed_never_written: An entry may NOT carry a confidence number. It carries the DATES it was confirmed and the dates it was contradicted, and scripts/carousel/instincts.py derives confidence from those events. Writing one by hand is a hard fail on load. This is the compute-not-generate law applied to the machine's own self-knowledge, and it is here because the sibling's ledger shows exactly what happens without it: 47 of its 101 entries sit at 0.90 confidence while only 25 entries have ever been confirmed once. Those numbers were typed by a model grading its own lesson, and a machine that can assert its own confidence will assert it high.
_spec.how_confidence_is_derived: Laplace's rule of succession, (confirmations + 1) / (confirmations + contradictions + 2). A brand new instinct scores 0.5, which is the honest score for a lesson nothing has tested yet. Three clean confirmations reach 0.8. One contradiction against three confirmations drops to 0.67. The rule is from 1774 and is not measured from our own corpus, which matters: a threshold derived from our own history is a ratchet, and one derived from lessons we already believe would confirm whatever we happened to write first.
_spec.injection: Before the directors room and the copy chamber, the run is handed the top 5 instincts at confidence >= 0.7. Under this formula that bar means at least three confirmations with no contradiction, so an instinct reaches the prompt by surviving three runs rather than by claiming to be important.
_spec.pruning: An entry contradicted more often than confirmed, once it has been tested at least three times, is retired rather than deleted. Retired entries keep their evidence, because 'we tried this and it was wrong' is a lesson too and re-learning it costs a run.
_spec.why_this_starts_empty: This repo has shipped zero decks. It cannot have learned anything from running, and seeding it with the sibling's 101 entries would be a lie about this machine's experience told in the machine's own memory. Those lessons are also about the sibling's engine and its art libraries, so most of them name files that do not exist here. Run 1 injects nothing, which is correct.

entry_schema.learned: YYYY-MM-DD, the run that first wrote it down
entry_schema.instinct: one imperative sentence, addressed to the next run
entry_schema.evidence: what happened that taught this, specific enough to re-check
confirmed: YYYY-MM-DD, one per run that saw it hold
contradicted: YYYY-MM-DD, one per run that saw it fail

entries.instinct: Answer a dead band with the object that belongs in it, never with a full field hatch.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, slide 8. The frame scored 0.75 / 0.87 / 0.66 on qa.py's band density with no warn WHILE carrying a 290px empty band all three judges named, and slide 7 scored 0.09 / 0.09 / 0.06 on a frame that was genuinely built. The metric counts cells over a contrast threshold, so it is fooled in both directions. What went in slide 8's gap was the lane a finished sheet travels down to the pins, with an empty landing at the end of it.

entries.instinct: When a rule is about what a reader SEES, assert it on the laid out geometry and never on the DOM string, because the string can be right while the render is wrong.
entries.evidence: Adding one citation to the foot pushed the row past its 920 px measure, the flex line broke, and the cover printed texasaidocket.com01 with the counter on a second line. All three judges opened with it. coherence_check reads the span and found texasaidocket.com, so it passed. Every frame now measures its own foot spans for wrap and gap.

entries.instinct: State which population a published count measured, because a number computed over the wrong set is worse than a typed one and arrives wearing the authority of a computation.
entries.evidence: 2026-08-22. The cover said 10 rows quoted when six were. The derivation counted index-row CLAIMS while the sentence described FRAMES. A note in the storyboard was congratulating the run for replacing a typed 8 with that computed 10.

entries.instinct: Make every count on a frame name the set it counted, and make that set one the deck actually read, because a bare count over a partly quoted index asserts a number nothing checked.
entries.evidence: 2026-08-22. 'The deadline sits in the index twice.' was the panel's only hard fail, over an index the deck quotes 10 of 34 rows from. It became '2 rows here carry the deadline.' and declared from c8, c9 and c10. Slide 4 carried the same defect one frame away.

entries.instinct: Read a gate's traceback as a finding about the gate rather than about the deck, and fix the gate in the same run with a self-test case that goes red on the old code.
entries.evidence: craft_floor raised ZeroDivisionError on deck 14 because the deck is entirely SVG, every canvas variance was 0.0 and the median it divides by was 0.0. A crash is not a verdict and it would have told the next SVG deck nothing either. Fixed to ask the same question of the band densities qa.py records for every frame, and it then did real work, failing the darkest frame for carrying 9 percent of the deck's own median.

entries.instinct: If a frame declares a real world dimension, derive the scale from it, because a typed pixel beside an unused constant is code describing work it does not do.
entries.evidence: Frame 6 typed PX_PER_IN 6.0 and RAIL_Y 640 against BASE_Y 1188, putting a handrail 91 inches above the floor, while RAIL_H_IN 34 sat declared and exported into the assert bag and used nowhere. A craft judge found it in the source twice. The scale is derived now and the rail diameter, the cove and the bracket count all fall out of it.

entries.instinct: Compute the drawn quantity's share and THROW unless it equals the arithmetic it depicts.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, slide 2, rounds 2 and 3. A 21 step density ramp with two knockouts read to two independent judges as two bars with the DARKER one SHORTER, inverting 34.82 against 51.16, and its most saturated block sat on the headroom that was not achieved while the frame's words were gated against naming a shortfall. Every numeral traced. The picture was the only thing lying, and nothing measured it. It is now ink laid down to the measured figure and an outline to the rated one, and the frame throws unless the inked share equals RMAX over RPEAK.

entries.instinct: When a gate enforces a number, make its test fixtures derive that number from the same source the gate reads. A fixture holding its own copy proves only that the copy matches.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, PR 252. ledger_check derived closing_moves_recent three deep off its own line while windows() read one out of CAPTION_CRAFT.md, and every self-test fixture typed three as well. All of it passed. A review bot found it by reading the two files side by side, which was the only way it was ever findable: the number the gate enforced and the number the gate derived were never compared to each other.

entries.instinct: State every craft floor in the unit a reader's eye uses, L star measured on the rendered PNG, because a fix can clear a floor in pixels and carry no visible difference.
entries.evidence: Frame 3's shadow ramp cleared 3 device px of offset per row and carried 1.5 L* of density over near black felt, which is nothing. Three consecutive rounds shipped a repair that satisfied its item numerically and was invisible.

entries.instinct: Every declared focal needs a DRAWING STEP and a measured value delta against the ground around it. A dossier naming a region the light extreme, with nothing in the script that puts a mark there, ships as ordinary bed.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, slide 9. The dossier called the open registration area 'the brightest region in all nine frames' and between the seated leaf and the dashed one there was nothing but hatched bed at the same value as the whole frame. The craft judge found it on the closing frame and named it as the artwork ledger's own avoid_next line repeating verbatim.

entries.instinct: Never label a drawn object with a count of the objects, only with what a source says.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, slide 8. A label reading 'TWO STATIONS, NOTHING SEATED' was rejected by aggregate_check as a figure computed from objects the deck itself drew rather than from anything a source states. Nothing in the record says how many institutions could be seated. It reads 'OPEN STATIONS, NOTHING SEATED' and is better for it.

entries.instinct: Never answer a quiet band with an object that could be read as the thing the frame refuses to say.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, slide 9. A graduated tick rule was drawn across the foot of the closing frame to answer a low craft density, and at 432px it reads as a TIMELINE on the one frame whose entire message is 'No date is published for it'. It was the single most misleading object this deck could have drawn, added for a reason that had nothing to do with meaning.

entries.instinct: After answering a composition gate, re-read the frame for what the new furniture now asserts.
entries.evidence: A dashed leader added to clear slide 9's dead lower zone ran from the no-action node into an empty passed-date field, which is a causal drawing and turned a record into an accusation.

entries.instinct: An idempotence guard on an append must fail loudly when it skips, because a guard that quietly does nothing turns a repair into a false report.
entries.evidence: The award number claim was appended under if c34 not in ids. c34 already existed as the NSF release claim, the write was skipped, and six frames spent a round citing a document that does not contain the number. Worse than the bug, the run reported the repair as done. The id is now read off the file with max plus one.

entries.instinct: Assert CONTRAST against the ground a mark actually lands on, never only that the string is present.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, slide 4, panel round 1. All three judges stopped the deck on one sentence. The dek's third line laid out below the sepia curl on bare cream while keeping its cream fill, at roughly 1.05 to 1. A ghost at 2160px and entirely absent at 432px. The sentence was 'No meeting date is published for that approval.', the only qualifier on a claim the claims file marks medium confidence and explicitly not a dated vote. copy.json carried the string because the browser really did lay it out, dossier_check's acceptance item asserted the string was present and it was, numeral_lint traced every numeral, qa.py returned zero fails, and panel_ready reported that every line cleared the rubric's 4.5 contrast floor while this line sat at 1.05. Twelve gates read what the document SAYS and none read what the page SHOWS.

entries.instinct: Print what the record was measured for, never what sources are said to have omitted, because one source speaking to one member refutes the whole sentence.
entries.evidence: force_unstated is items carrying no effective key date at all. Three frames and the caption printed it as 'no source says either way', and c44 in the same run's claims file is Wichita Falls saying 'We did prohibit evaporative cooling systems', on a fact frame 8 of the same deck prints.

entries.instinct: A script that certifies a published figure must run from a fresh checkout. If it reads only uncommitted scratch, nobody outside the run can check the number.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, PR 252. measure.py and measure_focals.py both read render/slide-NN.png and nothing else, and render/ lives under out/ and is never committed. The two scripts backing the compute-not-generate promise could not be re-run by anybody holding only the repository. They now fall back to the shipped frames, and because eight of nine are WebP the fallback agrees to about three tenths of an L* point rather than exactly, which the file states instead of glossing.

entries.instinct: Read a measurement script's BODY against its docstring before trusting either.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, round 5. measure_focals.py was written in round 4 to end the fault of typed figures claiming to be measured. It opened the PNG, computed a scale factor from its width, never used it again, and returned arithmetic over nine hardcoded rectangles, under a docstring reading 'the numbers come out of the pixels'. The craft judge read the source rather than the docstring, which is the only reason it was caught. Rewritten to actually read pixels it immediately found that slides 8 and 9 declare a small object as the frame's light extreme while 80 percent of each frame sits at that value.

entries.instinct: Reconcile copy.json against the render report's own text nodes rather than trusting copy_sync_check, which compares skeletons with every non-alphanumeric stripped and so cannot see a missing space.
entries.evidence: 2026-08-22. Seven copy.json strings disagreed with the laid out text and copy_sync_check was green on all of them. The staged build published '7/16/2026Fedor Mikheev' and 'September 4th, 2026.Refer' as article prose.

entries.instinct: A claim's own paraphrase can assert more than its quote, and every surface downstream inherits the excess with nothing able to see the gap.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-09, carousel 18. c13's text read 'Three named clinicians wrote the study' where its quote is a byline reading MD, BS, MD. A BS is not a clinician credential, so the caption said CLINICIANS on the widest-reach surface. Three judges found it. No gate compares a claim's text to its own quote.

entries.instinct: Scale every repeated object's values by where it sits in the light the ground already carries, and check the ground's own lit edges agree, because identical gradients on identical objects read as a texture rather than as a lit scene.
entries.evidence: Deck 15 frame 5 was fixed for this in round 2 and frame 7 shipped fourteen drums carrying one identical gradient at one identical height into round 3. Giving the drums a falloff in round 4 then left the plate's own lit top edge running the full width at one value, which is the largest element in the frame declaring where the light is.

entries.instinct: Answer a contrast or strikethrough failure by darkening the art under the type in place, never by laying an opaque rectangle or a full strength wash over it.
entries.evidence: Four plates went on in two rounds to answer QA findings. Slide 5 became 48 percent stacked black bars whose dek and foot plates shared a left origin and a right edge, rebuilding the shared axis that frame's law forbids. The replacement wash on slide 9 then covered the spill wedge and the two part contact shadow, so the cure reproduced the plate.

entries.instinct: Put the quotation marks on the FRAME whenever a slide prints a source's own string, because the site treats an unmarked row as this project's own sentence.
entries.evidence: 2026-08-22. Slide 7 printed three PUCT index rows unmarked. house_style_check failed the built article on the source's own abbreviation Sept. 4, a string this project never wrote. Slides 2, 3, 8 and 9 wore their marks and were exempt.

entries.instinct: Re-read the WHOLE frame after repairing part of it, not the part that was repaired.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, slide 4. Round 1 extended and darkened the plate so a lost sentence would read, and nobody re-read the attribution two inches above it. Round 2 stopped the deck on that line. A repair verified against the defect it was written for, on a frame carrying a different defect the whole time.

entries.instinct: Apply every copy repair to every published surface in one pass, reading them from one list, because a fix that lands on the frame a judge named leaves the same sentence shipping in the caption.
entries.evidence: Rounds 13 and 14 hard failed three times on one sentence. Round 13 failed frame 3 for 'Nothing in their sources says the action binds'. The frame was repaired and round 14 failed the run twice more for the same sentence on frame 6's foot and in the caption. Both round 14 judges' one-sentence fix was this.

entries.instinct: Re-run the deck-level similarity gate after every repair round, not only after the build.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, round 4. Three rounds of repairs had put one rect-loop idiom into several frames, and bespoke_check FAILED the deck at 0.5515 against its 0.55 line with slides 6 and 7 at 0.791. Nothing in the run had made the deck more of a template on purpose. Fixing frames one at a time with the same tool is how a deck converges without anybody deciding it should.

entries.instinct: Select the set a published count runs over from the record's own structured fields plus ids admitted with a written reason, never a regex over summary prose.
entries.evidence: tx-2026-0002 entered the counted set because its summary says the Texas Register text 'does not contain the words data center'. The regex matched a negation, so a published door count rested on a phrase saying the words are absent.

entries.instinct: Put every self-assertion a frame makes in a THROW, because render.py records an uncaught exception as a page error and qa.py fails on it, and nothing in this repo reads window.__txProbe.
entries.evidence: Deck 13's ledger entry describes frames publishing measurements to window.__txProbe. Nothing reads it. render.py collects text_nodes, rules, svg_plates, canvases, encodings, contacts, leaders, console_errors and page_errors, and a console error is only a WARN. Deck 14 put its counts, its geometry and its refusals in throws instead, and three of them fired during the build: a source rule 24px outside a punched opening, a dek reaching a sheet it had to clear, and a slot cut in the wrong layer.

entries.instinct: Where a boolean field would have to mean both 'measured false' and 'the question does not apply', give it a third state and suppress the question instead of answering it.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, PR 252. tx-2026-0118 is a federal request for comment on compute derivatives. It is nationwide, concerns a market rather than a facility, and names no state, and geography.on_ercot stored false printed a reader a plain 'No. It sits outside the ERCOT interconnection.' That is the compute-not-generate law applied to a flag: where it is neither measured nor modelled it is not published. Widening the field is a break, so SPEC_VERSION rose to 2 to say so.

entries.instinct: Write every acceptance item so that rendering NOTHING fails it, not just so that rendering too much fails it.
entries.evidence: Carousel No. 1. 'The stipple density stays low enough that the paper reads as tooth' passed on slide 6 where no stipple rendered at all, and 'the bottom third carries the densest engraved mass' passed on slide 4 where a flat warm wash was doing the work. Both items had a ceiling and no floor.

entries.instinct: Put one acceptance item on every dossier that names what the frame must NOT be mistaken for, because a checklist of parts passes while the whole reads as the wrong thing.
entries.evidence: Slide 5 passed all five of its acceptance items while reading as a Gantt chart that asserted start times the record does not state, with the contradicting caption on the same frame. The list checked edges, proportions, light and labels and never asked whether it read as a chart.

entries.instinct: A pre-meeting agenda book records what a body was asked to do, so never let a frame say it voted, authorized or amended without a source published after the meeting.
entries.evidence: The 2026-08-26 record and four deck surfaces said the UT System board acted on August 12th, citing the agenda book, which is a request. Correcting it needed a Community Impact report fetched after the meeting, and the error reached the scoring panel as a hard fail with every gate green.

entries.instinct: Register an absence as a first-class claim with its own id, the document it is absent from, and the search that failed to find it, because a sentence with no claim id is the one assertion nothing downstream can check.
entries.evidence: 2026-08-22. 'The rule as published in the Texas Register does not contain the words data center' ran on slide 2, in the caption and in the first comment while living only as prose inside claims.rejected. It is now c20, with occurrences counted in code from the fetched page.

entries.instinct: An acceptance item may require a frame to be positive, or specific, or scoped. It may NOT prescribe the word, because the fact will be bent to fit the word rather than the other way round.
entries.evidence: Carousel No. 5 slide 7. The item read 'says what each does PUBLISH rather than what it fails to publish', and the frame then said 'DPS publishes first responder interaction plans' where c34 says the page TAKES them and the absence record says it CARRIES them and a submissions address. Publish and receive are opposite directions on the one frame whose subject is what each page holds. The eighth panel's integrity judge failed the deck on it and named the acceptance item as the cause rather than the sentence. Fixing only the sentence would have left the instruction that produced it in the plan for the next run to execute again.

entries.instinct: When a gate passes because a feature has never been used, write its expiry into the assertion, because the run that first uses the feature is the one that can least afford to argue with its own suite.
entries.evidence: Carousel No. 1 turned two green assertions red on the same afternoon. The ask engine asserted no request leaves the page, which held only while runs/carousel was empty. The instincts self-test asserted the ledger starts empty since this repo has shipped no decks.

entries.instinct: Derive every source stamp from the URLs of the claims that frame's copy actually carries.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14. Three frames carried the same attribution defect and each was found in a different round: slide 4 credited c10's quotation to c8's publisher in round 2, slide 7 credited the docs page with a testing page sentence in round 4, and slide 6 set the chancellor's quotation with no publisher at all in round 5. Every fix was to the instance. Both round 5 judges proposed this binding independently as their one sentence fix.

entries.instinct: Answer a dead band in the register the deck already established, never in a borrowed one.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, slide 8. The band was filled with a dashed rectangle, guide rails and tick ladders, which the deck's own risk list bans by name ('no title blocks, no neatlines, no borders anywhere'), which was the only object in nine frames that was neither a sheet nor light, and which moved the band metric by 0.004. Redrawn as two empty seats on the same leaf module, outlined rather than filled, it says the same thing in the language the deck spent eight frames teaching.

entries.instinct: Check every attribution against the publisher of the claim that frame is quoting.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, slide 4, panel rounds 1 and 2. The frame declares c8 and c10. The quotation on it is c10's, fetched from tarleton.edu, and the attribution read QUOTED IN THE SYSTEM'S NEWSROOM, which is c8's publisher. The label was not invented, it was taken from the wrong one of the two claims the frame declares. It survived two rounds and the deck's own first comment contradicted it under the same post.

entries.instinct: Clamp any loop counter derived from TX.fbm2, because the field is SIGNED and a negative step makes a while loop that never advances, which the renderer reports only as a 45 second page timeout.
entries.evidence: Slide 7's stepped contact computed its run length as 44 plus fbm2 times 104. A negative sample made run negative, x stopped advancing, and the frame failed twice with a Page.goto timeout that named nothing.

entries.instinct: Give the deck one colour law that says WHO IS SPEAKING, and hold every frame to it, because attribution carried in the drawing survives a reader who never reaches the mono line under the figure.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 10's sharpest trap was the applicants' 525.5 MW figure that the order only records. Caliche for the commission and ochre for a party disarmed it in the drawing. A craft judge then found the law broken on four frames, which is also how the fix was found.

entries.instinct: Any position or length a reader could measure goes through compute.py, not just the ones that carry a printed number.
entries.evidence: Slide 4's stationing terminus was typed at x=660, drawing a 63:37 split where the hours are 81:19, beside ten minute ticks that were themselves to scale. The frame promised a scale and contradicted it, and no gate caught it because no numeral was printed.

entries.instinct: When a judge catches one typed figure claiming to be measured, GENERATE every figure of that kind.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, rounds 3 and 4. Round 3 replaced the storyboard's value arc after a judge found it asserting it was measured off the renders and being a guess, wrong on one frame by a factor of four. Round 4's craft judge then found four more of exactly the same kind in the same file, the focal shares, untouched: slide 1 declared about 11 percent and measures 44.6, slide 9 declared about 16 and measures 3.2. Patching the instance left the class standing for a whole round.

entries.instinct: Count the marks that carry ink, never the marks.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, slide 7. The frame asserted 1100 grain marks and drew 2600, and the craft judge found about a dozen visible at 2160px and none at 432px, because the spill term fell to zero below y 700 and left every mark in the lower two thirds at 0.05 opacity. The assertion counted nodes in a document. Nobody counted marks on a page.

entries.instinct: Derive a label's position from the same transform that draws the shape it annotates, because a label placed at the shape's untransformed anchor drifts silently and the drift grows with distance.
entries.evidence: Slide 4's three veins were rotated 22 degrees about their own left edge and their labels were drawn at that anchor, 750 px away. Every label sat 303 px below its vein, so the widths encoding 60, 30 and 10 minutes bound to nothing. Every gate passed. A craft judge said it could not tell which vein was the thirty minute one, which was the only signal there was.

entries.instinct: Draw every ground plane BEFORE the objects standing on it, and stop every drawn element above the footer band, because a plane painted last erases the object and leaves its shadow behind.
entries.evidence: 2026-08-22. Slide 7 drew a lit spine and its foot, then painted plane(1010,1350) over both. The spine died at the console line, the foot vanished, and a redrawn cast shadow ran through the texasaidocket.com glyph band. Slide 6 had the same defect the same run, three rods drawn and two shipped.

entries.instinct: Read every hook, dek, plate, the caption and the first comment into the quantifier register before scoring, because a hand written register only ever holds the universals somebody remembered to write down.
entries.evidence: Deck 15 raised the same defect in three different places across three rounds. Round 1 frame 9 'This test opens no comment period and no hearing', round 2 the plate 'PROGRESO, NO ROOM OPEN', round 3 'The way in is counted every month.' in 60pt type on frame 7, which quantifiers.json had never seen while it registered two other universals.

entries.instinct: Open the links a page you fetched names before you publish an absence that one of them could settle.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-08: the rejected list recorded that the agenda published no vote for the item, which was true of the page's prose and skipped the link titled Actions Taken By Council on that same fetched page. Opened after a judge named it, the notes record the item approved and publish no tally, so the deck's absence was right and had not been earned.

entries.instinct: Type knocked out of art must still be a real text node, because a word rendered as a hole in a mask is a shape and the PDF, the ranker and every copy gate lose it.
entries.evidence: Deck 14 slide 1 set its headline as a mask over two sheets. It rendered beautifully, passed the art crossing glyphs gate with zero failures, and appeared in NO text node in the render report, so copy.json could not carry it and the vector PDF held a shape. Setting the same words as HTML text in the bed's own value gave an identical picture with none of that lost.

entries.instinct: A document-structure locator printed on a frame must trace to a claim like a numeral does, because being true is not the same as being carried.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 10 printed six locators and none traced. All six were true when checked against the fetched order, which is why nothing caught them: a figure passes compute.quoted(), and a locator reaches a frame by being typed into slide HTML with nothing in between.

entries.instinct: When a word sits beside a drawn opening, advance from the OPENING's edge, not from the word inside it. The two differ by the opening's padding and the string is correct either way, so no gate can see it.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, slide 6, the thesis frame. The layout advanced by `w + 18` measured from the verb's own width while the slot already extended 16px past it, leaving a 2px gap. Two of three judges read 'willsupport' and 'willbe' on the frame the whole deck turns on. Every string, node and count was right. Only the distance was wrong.

entries.instinct: When a computation file and a frame disagree about a drawing, MEASURE THE RENDER before deciding which one is stale.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-09, carousel 18. A judge reported aggregates.json declaring 180 px per day against computed.json's 300. The run changed the declaration to 300 with a confident paragraph attached. The frame draws 180, so 300 was the number nobody drew, and the correction made the record agree with the half that had no pixels behind it. It survived two more scoring rounds and surfaced only when a knockout panel positioned from the 300 reading landed on the wrong row and struck a label.

entries.instinct: The turn slide must name its subject in its own hook, because a carousel slide gets screenshotted and reshared alone.
entries.evidence: Carousel No. 1 slide 7 opened on 'It is not in the queue' with the antecedent last named on slide 5. The flow critic could not recover the subject at feed speed until it reached a small label at the bottom edge.

entries.instinct: Give a new test case its own fixture name. Reusing the name of a shared one silently rewrites every case below it.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14. A new reverify case for escaped markup on an ordinary page was written as `page =`, the name eleven later cases read, and those cases then ran against a document that does not carry their quote. The suite crashed on the first one that indexed a key an unstamped item never grows, which is luck rather than a check. A case asserting the shared fixture still carries what the later cases look for is now the thing that catches it.

entries.instinct: Go back to the source for a plain sentence before concluding one would be an inference, because the law forbids inventing a reading and never forbade quoting a clearer one.
entries.evidence: 2026-08-22. Five scoring passes said the deck never told a Texan what the rule would do. All five were answered with 'that would be an inference'. The same Texas Register page carried a 54 million dollar cap and two plain conditions further down.

entries.instinct: Derive every cast and every lit facet from one stated azimuth by sin and minus cos, and never let a frame carry its own typed direction constants.
entries.evidence: Slide 5 of the 2026-08-26 deck ran on LX -0.62 and LY 0.78, which is 27 degrees off the deck's declared 246, and its lit facet was built from the first half of the vertex list rather than clipped to the sunward half plane, so the highlight sat wherever the polygon happened to start. The craft judge caught it against slide 2, the other overhead view.

entries.instinct: State a shared geometry ONCE in the builder and substitute it into both the canvas layer and the CSS layer.
entries.evidence: Carousel No. 3 slide 6. The four terrazzo bands were drawn full bleed at W/4 and the four label plates were laid out in a safe-area box inset 80px, so the outer two words straddled a band boundary by 37px. The safe-zone breach had been fixed on the type layer and the art layer was never told. The scorer measured it at the third pass; no gate could, because each layer was internally correct.

entries.instinct: Pin a copy box by its TOP and measure where it ended, never by its bottom.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, slide 4. A box offset from the bottom grows UPWARD when the copy wraps to one more line than anybody counted, and this one grew the other way off the sepia curl onto bare cream. Pinned at the top it can only grow downward, where a containment check can see it.

entries.instinct: Build any ImageData in DEVICE pixels and putImageData under an identity transform, because putImageData ignores the canvas transform and a CSS-sized buffer covers only the top left quarter of a 2x backing store.
entries.evidence: Carousel 16 slide 1 drew its bench as a 1080x1350 ImageData on a 2160x2700 canvas under scale(2,2). The unpainted three quarters kept the body background and rendered as a hard edged rectangle down the middle of the frame. render.py reported 0 errors and 0 warnings and qa.py returned PASS on the frame, twice. It was found by sampling the PNG along a row and measuring a step of 7 on values of 10 to 20 at x 520, which is exactly half of 1080.

entries.instinct: When a quote is cut short to dodge damage in a PDF text layer, check what the cut removed before shipping the shorter string, because the clause you drop is often the one a frame is about to draw.
entries.evidence: c6 was trimmed at 'point of interconnection' to avoid a page-break header the extractor had injected mid-sentence. The clause that came off named the shared settlement meter, slide 2 drew the meter anyway, and two scoring judges called it a fact with no claim behind it.

entries.instinct: After a repair, measure what it was aimed at and what it now sits next to.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-08: three times in one run. Moving frame 6's stock below the clause destroyed the frame's argument that the sentence runs out of page. Removing frame 7's swell outline was right and left the frame with no drawn object at 432px. Strengthening frame 6's centre crease put a dark band under type centred on the same axis.

entries.instinct: After admitting anything to the record, run the FULL site build by exit code before planning art, because the numeral gate's authorised set is site wide and a count you moved can expose a page you never touched.
entries.evidence: Admitting four items moved by_room open_meeting from 44 to 45, which un-authorised the digits in the campus name Project Gold Phase 2 - DFW44 on /construction/ and turned the build red at the point the deck was being planned. Reading the report's tail rather than its exit code had hidden it for two builds.

entries.instinct: Read the exit code of the BUILDER, not only of the checkers. A build that refuses leaves the previous build's output on disk, and everything downstream will happily process it.
entries.evidence: Carousel No. 5. build_slides.py was invoked with its output suppressed and its exit code unread. _footer_fit refused the run, correctly, naming a slide 9 byline 72px too wide, and exited 1 into /dev/null. The nine HTML files from the previous build were still in out/<date>/slides/, so the renderer rendered them, machine QA passed them, eleven carousel gates passed them, and three scoring judges graded a deck that had never been built. One judge caught it by comparing the render against the plan. The repo's own law says run a GATE by exit code; the gap is that the builder is not a gate and nobody had said to read its code too.

entries.instinct: Read every repair at 432px against the defect it was meant to cure, because a repair can be worse than the defect.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-09, carousel 18. A lit sill slab was added under the cover's doorway to stop it reading as a bare hole; a sill is the most window-defining element in architecture and all three judges then read the cover as a window. The same round's ambient-shadow fix on slide 6 clipped its own radial gradient and rendered two translucent boxes with hard vertical edges. Both passed machine QA.

entries.instinct: Sweep every fetched snapshot for the story's own subject noun before the directors room opens, and claim or reject every place it appears.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-08: the deck argued that City Code Chapter 2-19 merely weighed artificial intelligence and section 2-19-9 of that same ordinance lists the tools among what is not permitted. The run had cited six other sections of the fourteen page extraction. The ordinance names the subject in twelve places across five provisions and the run had read one. An integrity judge found it in scoring.

entries.instinct: Draw a shape seated INTO a surface with its shadow up sun and its lit walls down sun, which is the reverse of a drop shadow on both axes.
entries.evidence: Slide 6 drew a dark square offset down and right of each block and its dossier called it a recess. A craft judge read the frame as blocks sitting ON the face and marked artwork_craft 5.9. Measured after the fix, the walls read left 9.3 against right 92.1.

entries.instinct: Re-run the parser after any bulk edit to a file a gate parses, not just after editing its meaning.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14. Replacing the storyboard's curly quotes with straight ones per the house rule put unescaped quotes inside a double quoted YAML scalar, and dossier_check reported slide 6 rendered with no dossier at all. The edit was correct about the house rule and silently wrong about the file.

entries.instinct: When a slide claims one thing covers several, draw the covering thing touching them, with walls and an eave shadow, never as a wider bar above a gap.
entries.evidence: Carousel No. 1 slide 3. The roof plane sat 70px above the three stage planes with a black bar between, and the pixel critic read the whole frame as a four-bar SaaS chart. The acceptance item tested for vertical breaks crossing the plane, which a single rectangle can never fail.

entries.instinct: Run scripts/shared/guards_local.py in full before the first push, never a hand picked list of gates, because the suite reads guards.yml and a hand picked list is the half that misses what your own change broke somewhere else.
entries.evidence: This run pushed after running about a dozen named gates by exit code and CI came back red on docket_calendar's self-test, three assertions, caused by four expires key_dates this run had itself introduced. The full local suite reproduces it in one command and was run only after CI had already found it.

entries.instinct: A relationship between two sourced figures is a third fact needing its own claim, because asserting the arithmetic holds is a tautology that certifies nothing.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 10 printed '260 MW load + 265.5 MW generation' guarded by an assertion that the components equalled the quoted total. Every gate passed. The order's recital adds the two LOADS, so the 265.5 was a load and the frame called it generation. A judge caught it by asking which claim said so.

entries.instinct: A claim's text field is the run's own prose and only its quote is evidence, so a frame may print nothing the quote does not carry.
entries.evidence: Round 3 hard failed frame 8 for printing JOYDEEP BISWAS, THE CENTER'S DIRECTOR. Both halves came from the text fields of c24 and c25, which read the fetched page correctly, and neither quote contains the word director. The frame was repaired to attribute to the document. Nothing mechanical caught it, because both ids resolved and both claims existed.

entries.instinct: Compare the nine declared CAMERAS in the storyboard before any frame is built, because a repeated composition survives two rebuilds that change the geometry, the ink and the floor, and only changing the camera class separates the pair.
entries.evidence: Deck 15 frames 1 and 4 were the closest pair at 0.746 source similarity for three scoring rounds, both one point corridors. Attempt two changed the geometry from a superposition to one geometry at two depths and the pair did not separate. Attempt three changed the camera to a flat elevation and it did. bespoke_check measures the rendered similarity AFTER the build, which is the most expensive place to learn it.

entries.instinct: Assert source entailment over the claims file's own prose fields, not only over the frames.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, c19, panel round 3. Its text field read 'The System puts the same screening run at more than ten million compounds', on a quote published by Tarleton State that says nothing about it being the same run. So the record asserted the identity slide 5 denies on the frame in the deck's own voice, and credited the wrong publisher, which is the identical substitution that hard-failed slide 4 one round earlier, one claim away. Every gate reads the frames.

entries.instinct: Rebuild every artifact DERIVED from a thing you just changed in the same commit that changes it, because a stale derived file is wrong by construction and no gate is watching the gap.
entries.evidence: 2026-08-22. Committed new claims without rebuilding docs and the freshness gate went red. Committed a rewritten caption without rebuilding gmail_payload.json and email_check went red. Both were split off to clear a dirty tree.

entries.instinct: A deck's central line is written early, when the record is still thin, and then nothing re-reads it against the record that arrived afterwards. Re-check the HOOK against the claims file last, not first.
entries.evidence: Carousel No. 5. The cover read 'Every mile logged. No column for it.' over a byline of c27 and c28, a dateline and a mileage figure, neither of which supports an absence. The verified absence was narrower on both axes, a crash COUNT missing from three named pages, and the run's own rejected list says the TxDOT CRIS query never rendered and an absence cannot be asserted from a page that did not render. It survived four scoring panels, every carousel gate, a full pixel review and a flow critic, because each of them checked that the cited ids resolve and none asked whether the sentence above them says what the claims say. The sixth panel failed it. The cover now asks instead.

entries.instinct: Before a frame ships, check that every string set under a dated attribution is a verbatim substring of a quote in that slide's declared claims.
entries.evidence: Slide 7 of the 2026-08-26 deck printed 'clinical care, research, advanced computing' under 'BOARD ITEM, AUGUST 12TH, 2026'. That string is in none of the 31 claims in the run's claims file. Every mechanical gate was green on it and two of three panel judges caught it as a hard fail.

entries.instinct: Assert that a text repair CHANGED the file, because a replacement that matched nothing is silent.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14, rounds 4 and 5. The storyboard's arc note was reported reconciled in round 4 and the round 5 judge found it unchanged: the replacement string did not match and nothing checked that it had. The same run reported a slide 7 dossier reconciliation that also did not take. A repair reported as made and not made is worse than one not attempted, because the next round stops looking.

entries.instinct: Before a deck leans on a word a news story used, check that word appears in the document itself, because a framing adjective is a claim and journalism supplies it far more often than the filing does.
entries.evidence: Several outlets called the UT Dell Medical Center approved on August 12th an AI-native hospital. The Regents' own agenda book never uses the words artificial intelligence in that item, saying digital technology, robotics, and automation and a digitally enabled infrastructure. The whole treatment built on AI-native would have been a word put in a document's mouth.

entries.instinct: Before hand-editing a generated ledger, match the writer's own json.dumps arguments. A different indent reformats the file and buries the real change.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 14. Two repair passes rewrote ledger/docket.json at indent 2 where docket_build writes indent 1, turning a twelve line correction into an 11,778 line diff that no reviewer could read. The change itself was right both times. Nothing in the suite caught it, because every gate reads the parsed record and the shape was never in question.

entries.instinct: A repair that changes a computed value must walk every file that DECLARES that value, in the same commit, or the declaration becomes the next round's defect.
entries.evidence: Round 4 recomputed slide 6's dimension endpoints and left aggregates.json declaring the old 156 and 13 px at 13.0 px per month. Round 5's integrity judge found it and called it the identical defect rounds 1 and 3 had charged, made by the repair for it.

entries.instinct: Before the first panel, run EVERY gate in scripts/carousel by exit code, not the ones the routine's phase list happens to name.
entries.evidence: construction_check.py is in neither guards.yml nor the routine, so it went unrun until scoring round 3 and was red the whole time at 5 of 9 frames against a half threshold. The four decks before this one measured 2, 1, 4 and 1, so the finding was real.

entries.instinct: When an acceptance item names a MECHANISM, grep the frames for that mechanism before scoring. An item asserting a declaration nobody made reads exactly like one that holds.
entries.evidence: Four items on this deck asserted regions declared through data-encodes and data-contacts and no frame carried either attribute, so render_report's encodings and contacts were empty on all nine and plan_render_check passed anyway.

entries.instinct: Draw the subject before the type on every frame, at true scale, in one of ten rotated layouts, printed in paper and ink.
entries.evidence: Upgrade session 2026-09-11. Carousel no. 21 given full frame rects fails layout_check on seven of nine frames on detail or silhouette; the example deck built image first passes all six measures and qa.py with no FAIL.

entries.instinct: Measure every frame's median L star against the value its own dossier declared, in the same pass that renders it, because a declared value arc that nothing measures collapses into one band.
entries.evidence: Carousel 22 planned a sequence of 22, 46, 34, 30, 26, 18, 72, 26 and 28. It shipped measuring 11.1 to 41.1 with four frames within half a point of each other at the floor, and nothing found out until measure.py was written after the panel had already capped.

entries.instinct: When a variety ledger refuses a label, rewrite the work rather than the label, because the label is the only handle the gate has on the thing it protects.
entries.evidence: ledger_check refused carousel 22's build because the caption's opening move was inside its own six run exclusion window. Relabelling the move would have passed the gate and shipped the repeat it exists to stop, so the caption was rewritten from scratch on an unspent move.

entries.instinct: Run house_style_check straight after admitting anything to the record, because the Phase 7 instrument sweep does not carry it and a run's attention is on the deck by the time Phase 16 finds it.
entries.evidence: Carousel 22 reached Phase 16 with 12 sentences over the 30 word backstop, every one of them in the record's own prose rather than in the deck, across three admitted items, two re-verify movement lines and one claim text.

entries.instinct: When a pull request shows no check runs at all, first ask whether the branch still merges into its base, because a conflicted pull request gets no run rather than a red one.
entries.evidence: The September 12th and September 13th runs both failed to merge for two days. Both read an empty check list as something stopping CI. The September 13th run wrote a confident account blaming the session's credentials, built out of a 403 on workflow_dispatch that was real and incidental, and the owner had to point at the branch being dirty. git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD answers it in under a second and neither run asked.

entries.instinct: Never explain an absent signal with the one lever that returned an error message, because a thing that is silent and a thing that refused are different findings.
entries.evidence: No guards run existed on either day's branch. workflow_dispatch returned 403 Resource not accessible by integration, which was true and incidental, and it became the explanation purely because it was the only lever that spoke. The real cause was silent: GitHub cannot build a merge ref for a conflicted pull request, so the workflow had no subject rather than no permission.

entries.instinct: Merge origin/main into the run branch immediately before the Phase 16 site rebuild, so docs/ regenerates on top of current main and the branch does not go un-mergeable while its pull request sits open.
entries.evidence: Measured 2026-09-13 and corrected the same evening when a review bot checked the inventory. Four cron workflows run site_build and commit docs/ to main, eight pushes a day between them: news.yml four times daily, gridwatch.yml twice, datacenters.yml and generators.yml once each. A daily run regenerates the whole of docs/, so a run branch and main collide on generated files within hours, every day, with nobody doing anything wrong. The first cut of this evidence also named pages.yml and queuewatch.yml and neither writes to main. Rebuilding after the base merge resolves every generated conflict at once.

entries.instinct: Assert that a declared object is IN the frame at all, because every gate this product has measures what is inside the rect and none asks whether the thing the dossier named is inside it.
entries.evidence: Frame 1's figure was at X -13, which at that frame's camera and Z 9 projects to x -644, off the left edge of a 1080 px frame. layout_check --require, qa.py, plan_render_check, craft_floor, bespoke_check and a pixel critic all passed the frame. Two of three scoring judges found it independently, on three frames at once, and the cover's entire true-scale argument was missing.

entries.instinct: When a frame's job is to give a size, check the RATIO after the repair and not just the presence, because a figure moved into frame is a different check from a figure at the right distance.
entries.evidence: Frame 1's figure was repaired from off-frame to X -3.1 Z 9 and became plainly visible, in front of a building at Z 30. At 184 px beside a 16 m wall the frame then told a reader the hall was about 3.4 m tall, wrong by a factor near five. Round 2 caught it. At Z 27 and 48 px a judge measured the wall a reader reads off the picture at 13.3 m.

entries.instinct: Before planning a scene frame's median, subtract its reserve bands and its sky, because those two decide the number and the art has no vote once they pass half the frame.
entries.evidence: Frame 6 was planned at 14 and measured 3.8. Its art band was lifted from 4.4 to 10.7, the strongest of any scene frame in the deck, by rebuilding the caliche pad. The frame median moved from 3.8 to 3.8. That frame reserves 680 px of 1,350 for type and its sky is another 406, so 80 per cent of it is page ground by construction.

entries.instinct: Measure what a screen can actually lay down before planning a frame's value, because on a dark ground the press caps the frame and no drawing reaches past that cap.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-15, carousel no. 25. A dawn sky painted #D7AE79 into a cell 5 stipple came off the press at the same value as the ground beside it, and the deck's plan had asked that frame for a median of L* 40. Measured by printing a white field through each of the deck's own screen configurations: stipple 63.0 of 255, a ceiling of L* 26.7; hatch 107.6, 45.5; halftone 205.7, 82.7. The plan was 13.3 above the highest value that screen can reach with every pixel white. What must be bright is painted AFTER the press, which is the device the deck's paper frames already used for their sheet.

entries.instinct: Cure a dead lower zone with tone UNDER the screen, never with more objects standing on it, because a screen over a flat fill leaves every cell holding one tone and a few dark specks.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-15, frame 3. The near ground carried a hall, a figure, a truck, five bollards, four fence posts, a streetlight and two tyre tracks, and frame_balance still measured the bottom band at 0.237 of the frame's own craft density. The cells were live at 0.98 and their entropy was 0.31 to 0.52 against a modeled-tone threshold of 0.55: a stipple on a flat caliche fill is bimodal whatever stands on it. Grading passes and 1100 stones, each lit on one side and throwing to the other, moved it to 0.607 and the band ratio from 0.54 to 1.06 without adding a single object.

entries.instinct: Read every dimension an acceptance item sets AT FEED SCALE before accepting the pass, because a figure one pixel above its floor is a figure nobody can see.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-15, frame 3. The figure at the door measured 56.3 px against an acceptance floor of 55, which passes with a margin under two per cent, and at 432 px it was 22 px of white outline against a wall of other white outlines. A pixel critic could not tell it from door hardware, on the frame whose whole job is to turn a term into a size. The cure was not a larger figure alone: the door leaf is painted after the press as a flat lit rectangle and the figure is a SOLID DARK SILHOUETTE standing in it, because a dark shape on a lit ground reads at any size and an outline among outlines does not.

entries.instinct: Solve each frame's ground line from its own camera before drawing anything, because a subject whose ground projects below the frame foot is drawn and invisible, and every reader calls that absent.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 26 frame 4, 2026-09-16. The dossier declared a kitchen table with three figures and a tablet filling rect [0,340,1080,1010]. At eye 1.60 with f 900 the ground at Z 2.05 projects to y = 780 + 1.60*(900/2.05) = 1482, which is 132 px BELOW a 1350 px frame, so the table and both seated figures rendered off the bottom and only their heads were ever in the picture. Three scoring judges and a pixel critic each reported the declared subject as ABSENT and each reached for the lighting. Relighting cannot reach a subject that is not on the canvas. groundY = horizon + eye * (f / Z) is one line of arithmetic and it decides whether the frame has a subject at all.

entries.instinct: Draw a repeated unit ONCE and stamp it, whenever the deck's argument is that the units are equal, because three draws of one unit differ and a difference the source does not have is a rank the frame invented.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 26 frame 8, 2026-09-16. Three units at one depth under a long lens should come out identical and did not: the middle accent patch measured 86 px against 113 and 115 for the outer two, a 24 percent difference visible at 432 px, and the middle pair rendered 19 px taller. The frame's whole refusal is that the source ranks nothing, so the one saturated element on it was saying that one of three readings is smaller than the others. The repair was not a tighter tolerance, it was drawing one unit into an offscreen canvas and blitting it three times, after which no arrangement of the file can make them differ.

entries.instinct: Give a lit frame a light knockout plate and a dark frame a dark one, because the reserve is counted into the frame's own median.
entries.evidence: Deck no. 26, 2026-09-16. Frame 3 is a lit classroom in a 36 to 52 band and measured 8.1, because two opaque black plates and two black furniture bands covered about 42 percent of it, so the median was reading the furniture and relighting the room never moved it. Removing the plates took it to 74.9 in one render. But the same removal on frames 4 and 6 put light type on graded art and qa read strikethroughs, so the plates came back there, where the frame is dark and the plate agrees with the band. The rule is not 'plates are bad', which is what the previous instinct nearly said. It is that the plate's polarity has to match the frame's.

entries.instinct: Position every element BEFORE computing a reserve from it, because lineBoxes reads live geometry through getClientRects and measures whatever the element's coordinates are at the moment of the call.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-17 frame 9. '.card' was added to the reserve selector to stop the halftone running under the accent card's type, and the card is positioned after the canvas work, so the reserve was computed at its static position outside the tooth region entirely. The run reported the fix made and it was made in the string only. A judge found it by reading the code and the render together; every gate passed.

entries.instinct: Correct projection arithmetic is necessary and never sufficient. After fixing an object's geometry, look at it at 432px and ask whether a reader would name the object, because no gate measures recognisability.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-17 frame 3 across four rounds. Each round repaired a different symptom (no desk, no top face, a base missing the figures' ground line, mixed depths), the bench finally checked to the pixel at 1096.1, 1489.4, 873.9, 937.25 and PXM 341.67, and two round 5 judges still called the monitor a floor lamp and the empty chair unreadable.

entries.instinct: On a frame that quotes a document, check what it chose to set and where it stopped, because a lean is built from fragments that are each verbatim.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-17 frame 7, three times. Subsection (b) was spliced from two non-adjacent spans with no mark, which was a hard fail and stated the duty more broadly than the statute; (c) was truncated exactly where it stopped helping, turning an obviousness rule into a second duty holder; and only the pro-coverage reading was printed beside a closing question the fact-checker's rejection required to stay open. Every string was verbatim every time.

entries.instinct: Make the shipped slide source contain, as literal text, the strings copy.json says it prints, because entities a browser collapses pass the render check and fail the file.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-17 frame 4. 'SEARCHED    FOUND' rendered as 'SEARCHED FOUND', so copy_sync_check passed off the render's text nodes and shipped_check read the source and refused it. The fix cost a re-render after the scoring cap had closed, which is why this run's score row is stale.

entries.instinct: Run every sentence that CONNECTS two claims through the same test the quotes already pass, because no gate reads the prose between the quotes.
entries.evidence: Carousel no. 28 took seven scoring rounds and produced five hard fails. Not one was in a quote, a numeral or a claim: the claims file was exact in every round. All five were ordinary declarative sentences between the quotes. copy_sync_check asks whether a frame's words are declared, verbatim_check whether a quote matches, claims_check whether the claims file is sound, aggregate_check whether a numeral is computed. Nothing asks whether a sentence with no numeral and no quotation marks is supported, so 'the court posts one before every meeting', 'the county publishes these agendas itself' and a SPONSOR LINE label all passed the entire suite.

entries.instinct: When a surface has hard-failed twice, DELETE the sentence rather than rewrite it, and name the gap in the run record instead.
entries.evidence: Four of carousel no. 28's five hard fails were sentences added to give a reader something the run had not fetched, and each rewording produced the next failure. Rounds 2 and 3 are the same frame 9 line twice. Rounds 5 and 6 are the same addition twice, the second one written by the repair for the first. The fifth attempt is not better than the fourth. Round 6's repair deleted the caption line, and the deck shipped with the gap named rather than filled.

entries.instinct: Read what a gate CAN return before citing its exit 0 as evidence, because a checker that cannot fail passes everything.
entries.evidence: Three gates in this repo cannot fail and one run found all three. noun_trace ends with 'return [], warns, {...}', a hardcoded empty fails list, and its exit 0 was cited as evidence in four gate sweeps. The render harness collects window.__akLeaders, a sibling-project prefix, while these frames set window.__txLeaders. And leaders, rules, contacts, encodings, svg_plates and canvas_text are all empty on all nine slides of every deck this repo has shipped, so the declarative half of every acceptance list has never been machine checked. gate_wiring.py exists for exactly this shape and caught none of them.

entries.instinct: When a deck is about a public body, fetch the BODY'S OWN PAGE in discovery, not only the documents it published.
entries.evidence: Every scoring round of carousel no. 28 asked for something a reader could do. Three answers were written to fill that hole and two of them hard-failed for being unsourced. One fetch of the Hays County Commissioners Court's own landing page would have returned the meeting day, the hour, the address and the members' precincts. The run fetched the minutes archive on that same county domain and never asked for it.

entries.instinct: Ink a drawn figure against what is BEHIND it rather than against the palette, because a bright figure on a bright ground is the deck's scale argument made invisible.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-19 carousel 29. Four frames placed a 1.7 m figure at true scale and inked it M.G.bright, three of them standing against a cream data hall or lit caliche. The integrity judge reported that no figure was findable on five frames including the cover, whose entire job is to establish the scale the other eight borrow. The figures were all present in the code and all the right size. Inking them dark on frames 1, 4, 8 and 9 fixed it; frame 7's stayed bright because its ground is dark, which is the same rule rather than an exception.

entries.instinct: A catalogue sprite is a good object at the size it was drawn for and a silhouette at any other, so build a large subject from the frame's own projection instead of scaling a stamp up to it.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-19 carousel 29. TXOBJ.sprite('data_center') carried a 130 m hall on frames 1, 6 and 8 at three different distances, and its parapet motif rendered at all three as tall square merlons on a single cream fill. Three judges independently called it a crenellated battlement and one charged it as the weakest frame in the deck. Each of the three frames now builds its own hall from px(X,Z) and py(h,Z), differently, and bespoke_check improved from 0.5616 to 0.3748.

entries.instinct: A stripe that reaches both frame edges belongs to the FRAME rather than to an object, so give every drawn surface its own edges inside the picture.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-19 carousel 29. Frame 3's tailgate was a full-width rectangle with its ribs drawn as full-width rules. A judge read it as horizontal wallpaper stripes with no tailgate, no vehicle and no perspective, and was right: nothing in the drawing said where the gate stopped. Rebuilt as a trapezoid with its own side edges, converging ribs, swages and the bed walls behind it, the same object reads as a tailgate at 432px without a single new element being named.

entries.instinct: Register an absence as a claim with its own id while the documents are still open, because by the art phase it cannot be published at all.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-19 carousel 29. Both fetched documents establish that no count of unreturned water surveys is published, and the fact checker wrote that into the rejections rather than into a claim. Two scoring rounds later the reader judge's single fix was a line publishing the size of that gap, and it could not be written: an unscoped negative fails absence_check correctly, and there was no absence claim to scope it to. The deck publishes the gap in the state's own voice via c5 and publishes no size for it. The miss is at the claims phase, not at the art phase.

entries.instinct: Re-run every builder that reads a cite line the moment a cite line changes.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-19 carousel 29. Round 1 moved frame 1 onto c4 and frame 5 off c17 and c21 to repair a hard fail. first_comment.txt is BUILT from those ids by sources_block.py and nothing re-ran it, so the published sources block lacked the cover's own id and still carried two the deck no longer printed. sources_block --check exits 1 on exactly that and was not asked. run_state.json went on reporting it as exit 0, which was true of the deck before the repair. It cost a second hard fail and a whole scoring round.

entries.instinct: When a judge reports a DRAWING defect, change the drawing rather than the comment beside it.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-19 carousel 29. Round 1 was told frame 5's casts were 7px slivers against a comment claiming four times the height, and it rewrote the comment to describe the sliver honestly. Round 2 returned the same finding, called the repair out by name, and made frame 5 its one-sentence fix. Round 3 drew the casts. The honest comment was worth writing and it was never what the note was about.

entries.instinct: When a judge names a defect in one frame or one dossier, sweep the same class across all nine before re-scoring.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-19 carousel 29. Round 3 reported slide 8's numerals block declaring a claim that carries no numeral; the run fixed slide 8, and round 4 found slides 1 and 5 doing the same thing. Round 3 reported slides 7 and 8 both claiming an identical rect the drawing does not have; the run fixed slide 7's item and slide 8's rect, and round 4 found slide 8's acceptance still demanding rect identity fifty lines below its own retraction. Round 4's integrity judge wrote it as a one-sentence fix: every finding that round was an unswept sibling of the previous round's.

entries.instinct: After repairing a drawing, check the draw ORDER of everything added since, because a later layer can hide a fix as completely as the fault it replaced.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-19 carousel 29. Round 2 rebuilt frame 5's three casts because a 7px sliver was invisible at every size. Round 3 then added a raking ground apron across the same band and drew it after the elevations, so the hatch covered the wedges and the cast was invisible again for a new reason. Round 4's craft judge found it by reading slide-05.html's draw order against the render rather than by looking at the cast code, which was correct.

entries.instinct: Never put a command substitution between a command and the read of its exit code, because the substitution replaces it.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-19 carousel 29. The Phase 16 verification suite ran as a loop printing 'printf ... $(basename $g .py) $?' after each gate. Bash evaluates the substitution first and it CLOBBERS $?, so every exit code printed was basename's rather than the gate's, and basename was erroring on a two-operand call at the same time. The suite reported nine green gates and house_style_check was actually exiting 1 with 33 violations, most of them sentences this run had just written. It was caught only because a later rebuild happened to surface the same gate's stdout. This repo already has read-the-exit-code-of-the-thing-that-writes; that instinct is about WHICH command, and this one is about the shell losing the answer between the command and the read.

entries.instinct: Give a repair that makes a claim STRONGER the same scrutiny as a brand new claim, because the pressure to fix a real defect is exactly what smuggles an overreach past you.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-20, carousel 30. Three judges read frame 6 as a stacked bar chart and the anti partition argument was resting on 13px of smudged type, so round 3 promoted it to the 80px hook. It came out as 'None of these is a share of another', which is FALSE: two of the three counts are strict subsets of the first and this run's own figures.json says so under a key named small_systems_of_all. The run conflated 'the three do not PARTITION' (true) with 'none is CONTAINED in another' (false). Round 3's integrity judge refused the deck on it. The repair was correct in intent and the sentence it produced was a bigger claim than the one it replaced.

entries.instinct: Treat a judge's reported SYMPTOM as evidence and its stated CAUSE as a lead, because three judges can describe the same defect exactly and all name the wrong layer.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-20, carousel 30. All three round 2 judges reported the hatch screen 'running through every glyph' on frames 3 and 6. It was not. Both frames already painted their type flat in the print's over pass and frame 3's own comment said so. The SHEET under the type was screened at cell 6, and a 6px stripe under 15px mono fills the counters, so the letterform stops resolving. Fixing the reported cause would have fixed nothing. Their perception was exact and their diagnosis was off by one layer.

entries.instinct: Measure a repeated-draw helper's PEAK over its overlaps, never the alpha constant in its source, because a helper that draws one layer per element composites wherever two elements meet and the gate reads the constant.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-20, carousel 30. N.quiet painted one feathered wash per measured line box onto the same context. deck_chassis.py caps a fill behind display type at 0.55 and reads the constant, which was 0.44, so it passed every round. A craft judge computed 0.690 for frame 1's three line hook; the run then replayed the composite across all eleven line boxes that frame reserves, using the render report's own lines arrays, and measured 0.783. Forty two percent over a ceiling, on two thirds of the deck, under a comment congratulating itself for avoiding that exact arithmetic within a box while never looking across boxes. The fix is structural: accumulate coverage into one union mask with lighten, which takes the per pixel maximum, and lay the ground through it once, so the peak is the constant by construction.

entries.instinct: A declaration file written by the same run in the same hour as the sentence it certifies is documentation, not verification, so make it name the exact proposition and check that against the sentence's words.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-20, carousel 30. quantifiers.json was written to name the set behind frame 6's universal and marked it 'verified'. Its verified field argued that the three counts do not PARTITION a whole, which is true, while the frame asserted that none is a SHARE of another, which is false. Two different propositions, one file, same author, same hour, and the file read as a check on the sentence while defending a different claim. An outside judge caught it in one pass.

entries.instinct: Never draw two decibel figures as bars; print the source's own estimate, its own line and its own conclusion as text, because every bar encoding asserts a margin and only the source's arithmetic decides what the margin is.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-24 frame 7 went through three encodings. Linear bars from zero, energy bars against DNL 65 and equal bars against the 63.5 to 65 lift each drew a margin the draft does not state, and the last two each drew a hard fail from the integrity judge.

entries.instinct: Before writing that a document mentions something once, rarely or never, search the whole fetched text for the noun and cite or reject every hit.
entries.evidence: 2026-09-24 web edition said a person enters the draft in one sentence; the integrity judge found the Remote Pilot in Command and the approving customer in the same draft, a hard fail a text search would have caught.

entries.instinct: Point the deck's one key at the side of the hero every camera sees, because a key behind the hero turns white paint dark on every exterior frame.
entries.evidence: Carousel no. 34 declared its key at azimuth -160, which backlit the white tractor on frames 1, 4, 5 and 8. All three judges named the navy hero for three rounds until the key moved to azimuth 25, and the move then re-opened qa and contrast faults on four frames in the last two rounds.

entries.instinct: Set the world's haze from the horizon colour a probe frame actually renders, because a preset haze draws a hard sea band where ground meets sky.
entries.evidence: Carousel no. 34's blueHour haze read as a saturated band on frames 1, 3 and 9 through all five rounds, even after the ground plane ran to twelve kilometres. Sampling the rendered sky and setting the haze from it narrowed the band but came too late to clear it.
